points.description: States that a doubly-linked list allows insertion and deletion to be done in constant time (O(1)), including at positions before a given node or at the end of the list (because each node links to its previous node, no traversal is needed).
points.partial_credit: Award 2-3 marks if the answer says insertion/deletion is easier, faster or more efficient, or mentions backward traversal / previous pointers, without clearly stating constant time or the before-a-location/end cases.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying, in any wording, that insertion and deletion (including before a given node or at the end) take constant time/no traversal in a doubly-linked list. Give part marks for vague but on-track answers such as faster/easier insertion or deletion, or being able to move backward using previous pointers. Give no marks for answers unrelated to operation efficiency or direction of traversal; extra correct remarks are fine.
